name: app-6a7937f4b6708191b270a44fc2c4cf8c
description: Fix and improve your Shopify store's product feeds from ChatGPT, using the FeedShine app.

interface.longDescription: Fix and improve the product feed your Shopify store sends to Google Shopping, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Pinterest, right from ChatGPT. Ask why products are disapproved in Google Merchant Center and see the account and product issues ranked, worst first. Find the fields that are missing or weak across your catalog, such as product types, identifiers, images and shipping. Then fill a field for every product with one rule, or set values product by product. Rewrite titles to match the searches shoppers actually type, using your Google Search Console data, for up to 200 products in one approved step. Preview the exact rows Google receives for any product, take products out of a feed, and rebuild a feed on demand. Every edit is shown to you first and applies only once you approve it. FeedShine changes your feed, never your Shopify products. Requires the FeedShine app on your Shopify store, with AI assistant access turned on.
defaultPrompt: What is wrong with my Google Shopping feed? What should I fix first?
Why are my products disapproved in Google Merchant Center?
Which of my product titles miss the words shoppers search for on Google?

review.commerce_description: None. The plugin sells nothing and links to no checkout, payment page or app store listing. It only reads the store's feed data and edits the feed settings the merchant keeps in the FeedShine app.

positive.description: Orient in the store's feeds, then start adding a second store.
positive.prompt: Show my Google Shopping feeds and when they last ran. Then give me a code to add my other Shopify store.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists each product group's feeds with type, format, target market and the latest generation run, including item count and any error summary. Then returns a single-use code with steps to paste it in the other store's FeedShine app. No store is added in the chat, since that store's own admin confirms in the app.

positive.prompt: Why are my products disapproved in Google Merchant Center?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the account and item issues grouped by issue code with severity, how many products each affects and sample products, worst first, and suggests fixing account issues before item issues.

positive.description: Find missing feed fields across the catalog.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists every optimization section with how many products it affects, then drills into the worst section with list_section_products to show the affected products and the reason each was flagged.

positive.description: Fix a weak field for the whole catalog with one change.
positive.prompt: Some of my products have no product type. Fill it in from my tags for every product that is missing one.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads get_mapping_schema, proposes a mapping rule that applies a lookup over product tags only when the product type is empty and falls back to the default otherwise, shows the proposal, and applies it after the user confirms.

positive.description: Rewrite one product's title against real search demand and verify it.
positive.prompt: Improve the title of my Eucalyptus Grove Wax Melts using my Google Search Console data, then show me exactly what Google will receive.
positive.expected_behavior: Uses get_search_queries to find the product's highest-impression query and the words missing from its title (on the review store, “non toxic eucalyptus grove wax”, missing “non” and “toxic”), proposes a new title, applies it as an override after the user confirms, then calls preview_product to show the exact feed row.

negative.description: Do not trigger for orders, sales or revenue questions.
negative.prompt: How many orders did my store get this week and what was the revenue?
negative.expected_behavior: The app should not be invoked. It has no access to orders, customers, sales or revenue data.

negative.description: Do not trigger for editing the Shopify store itself.
negative.prompt: Change the price of my Ember Glow Soy Candle to 49 and update its description on my product page.
negative.expected_behavior: The app should not be invoked to edit the store. It changes what the product feed sends to Google and cannot write back to Shopify product records or the storefront.

negative.description: Do not trigger for ad campaign management.
negative.prompt: Optimize my Google Ads campaign bids for better ROAS.
negative.expected_behavior: The app should not be invoked. It builds and fixes the product data Google receives and cannot read or manage ad campaigns, budgets or bids.

publication.release_notes: 1.2.2 lets one ChatGPT connection cover several Shopify stores, for merchants and agencies with more than one. create_store_link_code gives a code that adds a store once that store's admin confirms it in the FeedShine app, list_feeds lists every store a connection covers, and every other tool takes an optional store. A connection with one store works exactly as before. 1.2.1 was the first release. It connects ChatGPT to the FeedShine app on a Shopify store to triage Google Merchant Center disapprovals, find missing or weak feed fields, fix a field across the catalog or product by product once the merchant approves, rewrite titles against Search Console demand, and preview the exact rows Google receives.
